question: On the same binary S_3 descent systems whose last fall degree d_F is known, what maximal step degree D_reg does an F4 run reach, and does it reproduce Kousidis and Wiemers' published D_reg (4 at n=34-36, 5 at n=37-48) on Semaev's polynomial subspace?

claims.text: On every instance, D_reg >= d_F (no F4 run can refute below the closure degree). A violation is an instrument or closure fault and stops the study.
On polynomial-subspace instances at n=34-48, our D_reg equals Kousidis-Wiemers' Table 1 value at the same n.
claims.if_supported: Table 6.3 can state that the published D_reg is reproduced on named instances and that F4 overshoots the closure at n=37-43
claims.if_not_supported: the published table and ours differ in a stated way (subspace, selection strategy or field equations); the paper reports both and does not merge them

claims.text: The gap D_reg - d_F per (family, n) is reported descriptively.

hypotheses.statement: F4 overshoots the closure by exactly one degree on polynomial subspaces at n=37-43.
hypotheses.mechanism: Our closure refutes at 4 there (P41a, P43a), while Kousidis-Wiemers report D_reg = 5; F4's normal selection strategy builds degree-5 pairs before the degree-4 span closes.

predictions.minimum_effect: D_reg - d_F = 1 on every P instance at n=37-43

arms.description: Boolean-ring F4 (crypto cryptanalysis::pq_f4_f2, normal selection strategy) on each .sys instance with the field equations; records every step degree.
Kousidis and Wiemers 2019, Table 1, m=2 rows (published values, not rerun; transcription checked against the PDF before freeze).
Instances with d_F = 3 (P17, R11, R13): F4 must refute with D_reg >= 3 and return 1.

aa.not_applicable_reason: F4 is deterministic for a fixed input and thread-independent in its step degrees; the closure protocol's A/A covers the shared build. A variable-order sweep would be a second factor, not a noise floor

positive.expected_detection: 1 in the basis on every d_F=3 instance

negative.not_applicable_reason: D_reg is a property of each system, not a test against a null population; satisfiable controls belong to FD-BINARY-CLOSURE-EXT

preflight_runtime.measured_on: pilot at n<=21 only (seconds); Kousidis-Wiemers report 188-103,200 s and 1.2-208 GB per n=34-48 in Magma. The engine caps one step at 2^27 words (1 GiB); a larger step stops the run as oversize (censored)

primary.name: maximal F4 step degree
primary.definition: largest degree of any F4 step until the basis is complete or contains 1

primary.name: F4 overshoot
primary.definition: D_reg minus the instance's d_F from Table 6.1 or FD-BINARY-CLOSURE-EXT

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design over the listed instances; n is run in increasing order and a cell beyond the memory or 72 h limit is censored
any C1 violation (D_reg < d_F) stops the study

invalidation_rules: a run stopped by its budget (timed_out) or the step cap (oversize) yields D_reg >= degree_reached, censored, and does not enter C2

decision_rule.text: C2 is supported at n when our P-instance D_reg equals the published value at n; it is reported per n, with no pooling.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: D_reg - published D_reg, and D_reg - d_F
